name: security-multipart-parser-boundaries-review
intent: Disagreement between multipart validation and the final part consumer
artifacts: Proxy/framework multipart parsers, duplicate-name selection, filename normalization and downstream upload/form consumer.
trace: Trace the same part through validation, binding and storage/use. Determine whether duplicate parts, encoding or nested multipart changes the value used after approval.
experiment: In an owned fixture compare one valid part with a single deliberately ambiguous benign pair and observe which marker each layer uses.
disproof: A duplicate accepted by all layers with the same interpretation is not a bypass; an unused parsed part has no demonstrated consumer.
repair: Use one canonical parser/selection rule and verify validator and consumer receive the same approved value.
branch_decisions: Record first/last/list selection separately for scalar fields and files. Filename and filename* normalization may diverge from ordinary field selection. Only the value used by the protected consumer matters; a harmless duplicate ignored by both validator and consumer does not establish a bypass.
operational_method: Preserve the raw bounded multipart body and each layer part inventory: part name/order, disposition, filename parameters, decoded value and file/field classification. Compare inventories with the value eventually authorized and consumed. Include a malformed-boundary rejection control; an echo of one selected value cannot prove all layers saw the same parts or that an alternate file part reached the protected processor.
